title: Swiss Re claims data: Waymo rider-only miles show 100% fewer bodily-injury and 76% fewer property-damage liability claims than zip-code-matched human drivers
summary: Heliyon (14 Jul 2024, Swiss Re and Waymo authors): Waymo liability claims benchmarked against 600,000+ Swiss Re claims; a Dec 2024 25.3M-mile update reports 88%/92% reductions.
account: The peer-reviewed Heliyon paper (vol. 10, issue 14, e34379; received 25 Apr 2024, accepted 9 Jul 2024, published 14 Jul 2024) by Luigi Di Lillo, Xilin Zhou and Margherita Atzei of Swiss Reinsurance Company and Tilia Gode, Ruoshu Chen and Trent Victor of Waymo LLC built a human-driver baseline from over 600,000 Swiss Re property-damage and bodily-injury liability claims and 125 billion miles of exposure (claims 2016-2021), calibrated to the zip codes of Waymo One's service areas in San Francisco and Phoenix, and compared it with Waymo claims from 1 Jan 2018 to 1 Aug 2023. Over 3,868,506 rider-only miles (no human behind the wheel) Waymo had zero bodily-injury claims against a baseline of 1.11 per million miles and 0.78 property-damage claims per million miles against 3.26, a 76% reduction; both differences had non-overlapping 95% confidence intervals. A follow-up paper posted on Waymo's site on 19 Dec 2024 (Di Lillo, Gode, Zhou, Scanlon, Chen, Victor; not peer-reviewed) extended the data to 25.3 million fully autonomous miles from 1 Jan 2018 to 31 Jul 2024 across San Francisco, Phoenix, Los Angeles and Austin, reporting an 88% reduction in property-damage and a 92% reduction in bodily-injury claims against the overall driving population (two bodily-injury claims observed against 26 expected) and 86%/90% against 2018-2021 model-year vehicles. The study authors note the baseline cannot exclude freeway miles and uses the insured's registered zip code rather than the collision location. The date given is the Heliyon publication date; the data cover the periods stated above.
purpose: The Waymo Driver is built to provide driverless ride-hailing; the studies were designed to measure its liability-claim frequency against human drivers.
system: Waymo Driver (SAE Level 4 automated driving system) operating the Waymo One ride-hailing service
deployer: Waymo LLC (Waymo One in Phoenix and San Francisco; later Los Angeles and Austin)
taxonomy_note: Crash and injury reduction is not among the six types; chosen as in AIBD-0008 because the measured gain is fewer third-party liability claims. Both papers are co-authored by Waymo staff; the Heliyon paper is admitted through peer review and because Swiss Re supplied and reviewed the baseline data. The Swiss Re-Waymo collaboration is described in the 25.3M-mile paper as non-paid and non-profit. Aggregate study, no individual event.

ratings.reason: Aggregate claim-frequency comparison; no individually attributable outcome is documented.
Fewer liability claims are reported in aggregate only.

ai_role.statement: The ADS drove all rider-only miles; claims were adjudicated by Waymo's claims administrator and the anonymized data were reviewed by Swiss Re, which built the human baseline from its own portfolio. The comparison is observational (different drivers, roads and reporting pathways), the rider-only sample in the peer-reviewed paper is 3.9 million miles, and Waymo authors co-wrote both papers.

evidence.title: Comparative safety performance of autonomous- and human drivers: A real-world case study of the Waymo Driver
evidence.quote: While driving without a human behind the steering wheel in RO mode for 3,868,506 miles, the Waymo Driver reduced bodily injury claims frequency by 100 %

evidence.title: New Swiss Re study: Waymo is safer than even the most advanced human-driven vehicles
evidence.quote: the Waymo Driver demonstrated better safety performance when compared to human-driven vehicles, with an 88% reduction in property damage claims and 92% reduction in bodily injury claims.

evidence.citation: Kusano KD, Scanlon JM, Chen YH, McMurry TL, Gode T, Victor T (2025). Comparison of Waymo Rider-Only crash rates by crash type to human benchmarks at 56.7 million miles. Traffic Injury Prevention 26(sup1).
evidence.title: Comparison of Waymo Rider-Only crash rates by crash type to human benchmarks at 56.7 million miles
evidence.quote: Data were examined over 56.7 million RO miles through the end of January 2025

produced_by: Geofenced, mostly non-freeway urban service areas in Phoenix and San Francisco
Liability claims adjudicated under state negligence law and reported for any incident regardless of automation level
A human baseline calibrated by zip code of the insured and by mileage exposure
Rider-only operation with no human in the driver's seat
must_hold: Access to an insurer's claims portfolio for the same zip codes and years
Comparable claim-reporting thresholds for ADS and human drivers
Sufficient autonomous mileage for non-overlapping confidence intervals
Operational design domain similar to the baseline's road mix

echoes.setting: Same method extended to 25.3 million rider-only miles (1 Jan 2018 to 31 Jul 2024) in San Francisco, Phoenix, Los Angeles and Austin; 88%/92% reductions versus the overall driving population

Police-reported crash benchmarks instead of claims: 56.7 million rider-only miles through January 2025; statistically lower any-injury, airbag-deployment and suspected-serious-injury crash rates (Waymo authors, peer-reviewed)

127 million autonomous miles through September 2025 compared by time of day and day of week in Maricopa, San Francisco, Los Angeles and Travis counties; lower any-injury and airbag-deployment involvement rates in all periods (Waymo authors, peer-reviewed)

headline: Waymo has zero bodily-injury, 76% fewer property-damage claims
metric: 0.78 property-damage claims per million miles against 3.26, a 76% reduction

revisions.change: Record drafted from the cited sources.

claim_basis: Two peer-reviewed studies from the makers, the makers' preprint and the makers' press release are on file. There is no independent source and no finding by a regulator or court.
